findings: Three condition-identical stories and 486 leaves already separate stability from confidence: stable-leaf mean confidence is .9643 versus .9095 on flipping leaves (gap ≈ .055), with pairwise agreement .8833, leave-one-repeat-out Brier .0643, and ECE .0290. Confidence is weakly discriminative and reasonably calibrated, not a high-resolution probability.

The observed-repeat equal-budget bootstrap is a direct negative result for extra spend: low-initial-confidence allocation was 1.742 accuracy points worse than uniform while raising the count of decided leaves. Confidence therefore predicts indecision/coverage, not a profitable accuracy return to extra samples.

Those two facts split the four product uses. Display is only a calibration/UX claim. Routing and resampling are budget-allocation claims and currently lose on accuracy. Abstention is a coverage–agreement claim and does not require new calls, new humans, or score mutation.

Leaves are nested in three stories, so leaf-level ECE/Brier overstate precision. Any operating point fit on all 486 leaves will leak story identity into the next test unless the unit of holdout is the story.

Automatic score weighting is unsupported: calibration of a binary decision is not evidence that confidence should move the rubric score, and the resampling loss shows that treating low confidence as a quality weight is the wrong direction.
recommendations: Run one frozen, story-held-out abstention test and treat the other three uses as locked no-ship arms. Do not start a new labeling round, do not reweight scores, and do not retune resampling.

Protocol: 3-fold holdout by story. On the two training stories, using leave-one-repeat-out only, pre-register a coverage grid {1.00, 0.90, 0.80, 0.70} and choose the highest confidence threshold that meets each coverage. Freeze those thresholds. On the held-out story, abstain below threshold and never alter retained labels. Average the three folds.

Primary endpoint (abstention): enrichment = P(flip | abstain) / P(flip | retain), plus retained pairwise agreement versus the current .8833 baseline, retained Brier/ECE, and coverage. Pre-register a ship gate such as mean enrichment ≥ 1.5 at coverage ≥ 0.80 with retained agreement higher than full-set agreement in at least 2 of 3 story folds. Secondary: fraction of flipping versus stable leaves removed. No accuracy-on-scores endpoint.

Display arm (measurement only): on retained leaves, report ECE/Brier and the stable-versus-flip confidence gap. Do not ship numeric confidence. If the abstention gate passes, the smallest display follow-on is a three-band map (high/mid/abstain) using the same frozen thresholds, still not shown as a percent.

Routing arm (measurement only): at each frozen coverage, compare flip-capture of sending the low-confidence slice to a held-out repeat versus a same-size random slice. Routing may ship later only if it beats random on flip-capture; it may not ship on accuracy, which already failed.

Resampling arm (negative control only): recompute the equal-budget bootstrap inside each story fold. Keep uniform one-pass as default unless the −1.742 accuracy gap reverses in at least 2 of 3 folds. More decided leaves is not a pass.

Report decided-leaf rate and agreement as separate columns so coverage gains cannot be mistaken for quality gains. Keep a single pre-registered threshold rule; do not search per-leaf or per-criterion cutoffs in this test.
risks: N_stories = 3 makes any threshold fragile; a win on two stories and a loss on one is the expected noise pattern, not a product signal, unless gates are fold-based.
The .055 confidence gap is small relative to .964 vs .910 means, so many flips sit in the high-confidence mass and abstention at high coverage will miss them.
Pairwise agreement of .8833 already implies that displayed high confidence will be wrong on a non-trivial slice; numeric display will overtrust even with ECE .0290.
Routing and resampling are easy to smuggle back in as “just one extra pass on uncertain leaves,” which is the policy that already cost 1.742 accuracy points.
Story-level style, length, or rubric difficulty can masquerade as calibration; leaf i.i.d. bootstrap CIs will be too tight.
Creative-writing binary leaves are dependent within a story; abstention that drops whole hard stories will look like a calibration win and a product failure.
If display, routing, abstention, and resampling share a live threshold, a coverage win will be misread as permission to spend or to weight scores.
output.summary: Confidence on this binary creative-writing rubric is weakly aligned with repeat stability and modestly calibrated, but extra allocation to low-confidence leaves already lost 1.742 accuracy points versus uniform. The next smallest product test is a 3-fold story-holdout freeze of abstention thresholds on the existing 486 leaves, with display/routing/resampling locked as measurement-only and scores left unweighted. Ship nothing but “abstain below a pre-registered coverage cut” unless enrichment and retained agreement beat the .8833 baseline without new humans or extra samples.
